<a id="consolemirror"></a>

## `ConsoleMirror`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Logging.ConsoleMirror` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

The one console sink. Subscribes to [`TraceBus`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Bus.md#tracebus) before anything else logs, decides per event whether it is console-worthy, and prints the canonical line SYNCHRONOUSLY on the thread that published it - so the order of the console equals the order of the events, and the stamp on the line is the event's own time.

Before this sink existed, the console copy of a bus event was formatted and printed by the trace plugin's writer thread. Live events lagged by a millisecond or so; the pre-attach replay was stamped at enqueue time and landed 4.6 s late, so the two sinks disagreed about when the same event happened. The trace file's copy still goes through the writer thread - that is where the frame-time budget was won - but the console copy no longer does.

This class decides nothing about the layout: [`ConsoleEventMap`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.md#consoleeventmap) owns that, and producers own their own tag, primary and field order. The mirror never parses free text.

<a id="consolemirror--install"></a>

### `static void Install()`

Subscribes to the bus. Call once, first thing in [`ModLoaderPlugin`](CwyLs.ModLoader.md#modloaderplugin).Awake: everything published before this point reaches the trace file but not the console. Calling it twice is a no-op.

<a id="consolemirror--print"></a>

### `static void Print(ConsoleRecord record)`

Prints one record now, on the calling thread. The only way a console line is written: the bus subscription uses it, and so do the few lines the trace plugin owns itself (clicks, UI actions, its own status).

**Parameters**

- `record`: The record. Null is ignored.

<a id="consolemirror--uninstall"></a>

### `static void Uninstall()`

Stops mirroring. Used by shutdown; safe to call when not installed.

<a id="cwyconsolelistener"></a>

## `CwyConsoleListener`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Logging.CwyConsoleListener` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

Implements: `IDisposable`, `ILogListener`

Writes every CWY log line (and every Error/Fatal from any source) to `BepInEx/cwy-console.log` in the canonical grammar: one physical line per event, stamped with the event's own time.

Two F3 fixes live here.

- The file used to be opened with `FileMode.Create`, so every launch destroyed the previous session - including the session a bug report was about. The previous file is now rolled to `cwy-console.<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.log` (the last [`CwyConsoleListener.KeptRolls`](#cwyconsolelistener--keptrolls) are kept) and the live file is opened for append.
- A line that is already a [`ConsoleRecord`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.md#consolerecord) is written as it stands. A direct `LogWarning`/`LogError`/`LogInfo` is wrapped into one, so the file has exactly one grammar and `tools/mac/watch-log.py` needs exactly one regex.

<a id="cwyconsolelistener--ctor"></a>

### `CwyConsoleListener(string path)`

Opens the console file, rolling the previous session out of the way first.

**Parameters**

- `path`: Full path of `cwy-console.log`.

**Parameters**

<a id="cwyconsolelistener--wrap"></a>

### `static ConsoleRecord Wrap(string text, LogLevel level, string source)`

Turns a line that was logged directly (not through [`ConsoleMirror`](#consolemirror)) into a record. A warning becomes `WARN`, an error `ERROR`, and anything else is a feature's startup summary - `SETUP` - with `src=` naming the plugin.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The logged message.
- `level`: BepInEx level of the message.
- `source`: BepInEx source name, e.g. `CWYLS Game Adapter`.

## `TraceSwitch`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Logging.TraceSwitch` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

RP-1: the handle the `trace` console command uses to read and change the trace. The trace plugin registers it in its `Awake`; the command used to look the plugin up through its component, which the game destroys about 0.2 s after boot.

<a id="traceswitch--register"></a>

### `static void Register(ConfigEntry<TraceLevel> level, Func<TraceLevel> running, Action stopNow)`

Called once by the trace plugin.

**Parameters**

- `level`: The bound `[Trace] Level` entry.
- `running`: What this session is recording right now.
- `stopNow`: Stops a running trace at once.
